Assessment.content: Acute gastroenteritis, likely viral versus bacterial, characterized by three days of watery diarrhea six to seven times per day, left lower quadrant crampy intermittent pain, brief vomiting now resolved, no blood, tolerating oral intake, and possible foodborne trigger from takeaway
Assessment.source_text: 1) Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral vs bacterial) — 3 d watery diarrhea (6–7/day), LLQ crampy intermittent pain, brief vomiting now resolved, no blood, tolerating PO; possible foodborne trigger (takeaway).

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise oral hydration with oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte
Paracetamol two tablets up to four times per day as needed for fever or weakness
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Paracetamol 2 tabs up to 4x/day PRN fever/weakness

Plan_of_Care.content: Recommend rest and time off work for 2–3 days
If not improved in 3–4 days, follow up and consider stool studies
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • F/U if not improved in 3–4 d; consider stool studies

Follow_up_Information.content: Follow up if not improved in 3–4 days for possible stool studies
